title: Forks with pawns and queens, and when they fail
outcomes: Finds pawn forks and queen forks
Checks whether the forking piece can be captured
Checks whether taking the second target gains material
Says when a check or attack is not a winning fork

steps.text:
Any piece can fork. A **pawn** fork is the hardest to meet, because the forked pieces have a higher counting value than the pawn. A **queen** can fork a king and a loose piece with one check.
Look for two targets that one piece could attack from a single safe square.

steps.caption: White to move. Which pawn move hits two pieces?

line.say: The pawn gives check and attacks the rook on e6 as well.
The king steps aside. The rook is still attacked.
The pawn takes the rook. White has won a rook for a pawn at least.

claims.statement: f5+ wins the rook for a pawn along the engine line.

steps.text:
Not every fork works. Before you play one, ask:
**Can the forking piece be captured?** By a piece, or even by one of its own targets.
**Does taking the second target gain material?** If it is defended and the forking piece has the higher counting value, the fork wins nothing.
Then check what your opponent can do instead.
